scope: Actual Metal compute output to RAM lease, disk swap and full-size rendering, compared with CPU float exposure oracle
checks: All CPU-computed exposure component bits match GPU compute readback
Compute GPU credit released after readback
Original source releases its CPU credit before cached frame ownership
RAM consumer lease prevents shrinking below retained frame
Every full-size Metal output pixel equals independently CPU-exposed raster before RAM insertion, through lease and after disk restore
Every float bit unchanged after disk restore
Exactly one disk write/read per case, zero swap errors
Managed CPU, compute GPU and swap queue budgets return to zero
multi_dispatch_budget_note: 12 MP initially refused the old single-uniform test allowance: requested 576000048 vs limit 576000016. Updated test allowance includes up to four 16-byte dispatch uniforms; no production change or fallback.
limitations: Authored float exposure inputs do not qualify all RAW decoding or all 100 formats
Full output readback is RGBA8 SDR, not physical HDR; separate float-attachment tests cover retained HDR values
Oracle vectors and display readback/driver allocations are outside named compute/CPU/queue budgets
Finite pipeline checks are not a long-running compute collection soak
Hour-long collection test remains in progress and is not counted as completed
Timings include concurrent GPU workload and are not isolated speed benchmarks
